items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: Well he was a loud trumpet player too.

ctx.x: Well, he had a little bit of tone, yeah, because he was taught, you know. He was a good teacher, you know. After he knew the fundamentals, you know, up to the horn, you know. Do you remember Joe Oliver? Well Joe come up, just like those other fellas, you know, starting out like that. I remember when I first saw him, I was playing with that Eagle band then. And we was playing on Rampart Street one night, just the trombones and the violin and the guitar and bass. So he came in this place with his horn, you know,…
Do you remember much about Freda Cuppert? I remember about Freda.

He was a, first he started on the violin, see, picking, you know. And then he picked up the trumpet, see. Well he was a loud trumpet player too. Well he played good too, you know what I'm saying? But he wasn't much in reading, you know, but he could play, you know what I'm saying? He had kind of a gift, you know what I'm saying? Something like Bechet, you know, gifted, you know.

items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: You take Bolden and, say, Freddie Keppert, now he died in Chicago. They were mostly on the same style.

ctx.x: What about Bolden? Does anybody who's made records or who's around today play anything like him?

Well, I don't know. It's practically, you take certain types now. You take Bolden and, say, Freddie Keppert, now he died in Chicago. They were mostly on the same style. They were powerful trumpet players and they mostly, well, the improvisation is always going to be a little different, you know, and they're no two men alike, you understand? But it's the similarity there, you understand what I mean, between them and the style was just a forceful trumpet player, you understand? Just strong and came out.
